result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by wide but poorly maintained sidewalks and a signalized intersection with significantly faded crosswalk markings. The lack of dedicated pedestrian signals and the presence of sidewalk clutter like ice machines and trash bins reduce the overall safety and accessibility of the area.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk lines are extremely worn and barely visible, which may lead to drivers failing to yield to pedestrians.

hazards.name: Poor Roadway and Sidewalk Pavement
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven pavement surfaces create trip hazards for pedestrians and may cause vehicles to swerve.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the roadway and left-side sidewalk

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: An ice machine and trash receptacles narrow the effective walking width on the left sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image in front of the corner store

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style high-visibility crosswalk markings to improve pedestrian visibility to motorists.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The image depicts a signalized urban intersection with high-visibility zebra crosswalks and wide sidewalks. While basic infrastructure is present, the environment lacks physical traffic calming measures, and sightlines are partially obstructed by parked vehicles near the crossing.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb near the intersection can obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway along the curb line

hazards.name: Large Vehicle Blind Spots
hazards.description: A large box truck is approaching the crosswalk, which typically has significant blind spots for pedestrians directly in front or to the side.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway approaching the crosswalk

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extending the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Removing parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Programming the traffic signal to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light, increasing their visibility in the crosswalk.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized urban intersection with marked crosswalks and sidewalks on all sides. While basic infrastructure is present, the environment lacks pedestrian-specific safety features like curb extensions or dedicated signals, and parked vehicles near the corners may obstruct sightlines.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars near the intersection corners block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sides of the intersection

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible to guide crossing timing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sightlines.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers.

result.summary: The intersection features a high-visibility continental crosswalk and overhead traffic signals in a mixed-use urban environment. While basic infrastructure like sidewalks and bike lanes are present, the wide crossing distance and lack of pedestrian refuge islands or curb extensions increase exposure risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for a significant duration without a mid-point refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb may obstruct the view between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the curb line

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow for safer two-stage crossing.
